page: Microsoft Azure M416ms_v2 is an ultra-high-memory instance within the MSv2 family, architected for multi-terabyte in-memory processing. It is built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon 8487C processors, supplying 416 dedicated vCPUs across 208 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled and base clock capabilities up to 4.0 GHz. The processor includes 105 MB of L3 cache, backed by 11,400 GB of system memory, which yields an allocation of 27.4 GB per core. Local storage is provided through a bundled 8,796 GB solid-state drive. Hardware acceleration via dedicated GPUs is not present on this machine type.

Benchmark data illustrates substantial multi-core scaling alongside high memory bandwidth. In parallel computing assessments, the instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core metrics (279,384.01) and PassMark CPU calculations, including hardware-accelerated encryption and extended instruction tests. Memory throughput reaches 691.64 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 320.33 GB/sec for writes, sustaining 290.37 million Redis SET operations per second and high static web throughput. Conversely, single-threaded processing is constrained, showing weak performance in single-core stress-ng, Geekbench, and gzip compression tests.

The platform delivers density for organizations consolidating extensive in-memory workloads into single-node footprints. Qualitative cost efficiency is realized through the extreme concentration of physical memory and compute cores, reducing multi-node clustering overhead. However, workloads dependent on single-threaded frequency or specialized graphics acceleration represent poor architectural fits. The instance is targeted at massive relational and non-relational database installations, including SAP HANA, large Redis caching tiers, and memory-constrained analytical data pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure M416ms_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for extreme-scale enterprise workloads. Running on the x86_64 architecture with Intel Xeon 8487C processors, it provides 416 dedicated vCPUs across 208 physical cores clocked at up to 4.0 GHz, coupled with 105 MB of L3 cache. System memory totals 11,400 GB, equivalent to 27.4 GB per core, and is accompanied by an 8,796 GB local solid-state drive with no GPU accelerators. In benchmark testing, the platform produces top-tier multi-threaded compute results and memory bandwidth exceeding 691 GB/sec for large uncached reads, driving over 290 million Redis SET operations per second. Single-threaded metrics rank lower, indicating that performance relies on wide parallelism. The server is well aligned with multi-terabyte in-memory database engines, expansive caching infrastructures, and intensive batch transformation workloads.
